steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since you finished your laser treatments with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still smooth, a little regrowth starting, or pretty much back to shaving. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Smooth
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes treatment with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still happy with the results.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

(Do not offer anything yet. Update the file first.)

steps.title: A Little Regrowth
steps.content:
That happens, {{contact_first_name}}, and it doesn't mean the treatment didn't work. Hair grows in cycles, and each session only catches the hairs growing that day. The ones you're seeing now were resting back then, or they're new. Your notes say you were really happy with how smooth it was. Does that sound right?

(Let them confirm. Stay warm. This is routine, not a failure.)

(Do not offer anything yet. Update the file first.)

steps.title: Pretty Much Back to Shaving
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. That's frustrating, and there's a real reason for it. The hairs we treated are gone for good. Over time, though, new ones can start growing in. It's not that the treatment failed. Your notes say you were really happy with the areas we finished. What kept you from coming back in?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. The progress they made is still theirs.)

(Do not offer anything yet. Update the file first.)

steps.title: One More Thing: Other Areas
steps.content:
Perfect, you're all set for (day) at (time).

(If you already covered other areas during the file update, skip the question. Confirm the appointment and end the call.)

One quick thing while I have you, {{contact_first_name}}. Once one area is done, people usually start noticing the others. Is there anywhere else you're still shaving or plucking?

(Let them answer.)

(If yes, read the next line.)

That's really common. I'll make a note so {{provider_name}} can talk it through with you when you're in. No commitment, just worth a look.

(If no, read the next line.)

No problem. I always ask, because a lot of people don't realize we can treat almost anywhere. We'll see you (day) at (time), {{contact_first_name}}. Have a great day.

(Either way, end the call with the appointment confirmed.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm updating your file anyway. Can I ask you a few quick questions so it's up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to the regrowth in a moment. First, can I ask you a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, the areas we treated. Any regrowth at all, even a stray hair or two?

How has the skin been in those areas, any irritation or ingrowns?

Next, a few spots people are often still shaving. Your underarms?

Your legs?

The bikini line?

Any on your face?

Your back?

Is there another treatment you've been curious about?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one would you most like to be done with?

(Tap their answer below. If nothing came up, that's still a good call. Use the second button.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, the regrowth. Where are you seeing it most?

How has the skin been in those areas, any irritation or ingrowns from shaving?

Next, a few spots people are often still shaving. Your underarms?

Your legs?

The bikini line?

Any on your face?

Your back?

Is there another treatment you've been curious about?

(Recap what you wrote down, including the regrowth, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between the regrowth and anything else you mentioned, which one would you most like to be done with?

(Tap their answer below. If catching the regrowth is the whole story, use the second button.)

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been on your mind a while, and you notice it most times you look in the mirror. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: photos, going out, or feeling put together. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

And it sounds like you'd like to get back to not having to think about it. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask a few quick questions about {{main_concern}} so your file is up to date. It'll only take a minute.

(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a few weeks, or more like months?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you notice now and then, or every time you look in the mirror?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with photos, going out, or feeling put together?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{main_concern}} is something you'd like to feel better about. I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Do not repeat the concern back at them. Let them answer.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look and talk through {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Stay Ahead of It
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad you're still happy with the results.

One thing before I let you go. Hair grows in cycles, and every so often a few new hairs start up in an area we treated. It always starts as a stray hair or two. They show up so slowly that most people don't notice until it's real regrowth. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes. If they hesitate, use the second button.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for one quick touch-up session. That way those few stray hairs never turn into real regrowth. Does that sound reasonable?

(Wait for the yes.)

Okay, let's find you a time. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Regrowth Is the Whole Story: The Close
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, thank you for that. Your file is up to date.

The good news is this is what touch-up sessions are for. We don't start from zero. It's a fraction of what you did the first time, and every session puts you further ahead. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for one quick touch-up session now, while those new hairs are active. Then you're right back to smooth. Does that sound reasonable?

(Wait for the yes.)

Okay, let's get you back on the books. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: “I thought it was supposed to be permanent”
steps.content:
That's a fair question. Laser removal reduces hair for good, but some regrowth can happen over time. Hormones can play a part, and so can an unfinished series. That's why coming in makes sense, so we can look at the whole picture and make a plan.

Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “I’m frustrated it came back”
steps.content:
I understand, and please don't be hard on yourself. Some regrowth is common, and that's the reason we call. We'd just like to help you get back to where you were.

Would you be open to that?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “Did it even work last time?”
steps.content:
That's a fair question, and it's the kind of thing we'd want to talk through in person. That way we can look at the whole picture and see what would help it hold.

(Do not promise results or permanence on the call.)

Is there anything else on your mind?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's right for them.

(Listen. Their answer usually points to one of the other objections. If it stays general, keep going.)

Coming in is really just information. You'd see what's possible and what it would involve, and then you decide with real answers. No pressure either way.

Does that help?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I'd be glad to send you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't show you what's possible for you specifically. That's what a quick visit is for. So let me get you on the schedule first, and then I'll send the information along.

Is that okay?
